items.X_desc: Give 10 when the caption implies a specific unseen event, history, or consequence that makes the pictured moment newly funny; give 0 when it adds no temporal or narrative information.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 if the caption trusts the reader entirely, dropping a punchline without spelling out the premise or the joke; score 0 if the caption painfully spells out the joke, uses unnecessary dialogue tags, or points out the surreal element too directly.

items.X_name: Purposeful edgy/taboo content (sexual, dark, or transgressive)

items.Y_desc: Score for content that is morbid, bodily, sexual, or ethically uncomfortable, delivered in a flat conversational register with no apology or wink. 10 = genuinely edgy material said as though it were small talk. 5 = mildly impolite. 0 = entirely wholesome content, or edgy content that is signposted, leering, or delivered with visible relish. Score the presence and deadpan handling of the transgression; do not penalize the caption for being impolite and do not reward mere shock without the flat delivery.

items.X_desc: Score 10 when a sound, spelling, or word substitution is precise, immediately recoverable, and tightly tied to the cartoon; score 0 when the wordplay is approximate or strained.
items.Y_desc: Give 10 when a sound or spelling resemblance creates a clear second meaning tied to the depicted subject without awkward stretching; give 0 when the resemblance is forced or absent.

items.X_name: Comic economy: punch lands with minimal, load-bearing words
items.X_desc: Score how tightly compressed the caption is in achieving its comedic effect, with essentially no throat-clearing, hedging, or explanatory padding, ending on the load-bearing punch word. 10 = extremely compressed, every word necessary, caption ends on the punch; 0 = padded or explanatory phrasing dilutes or delays the punch.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 if the caption achieves a massive conceptual twist using very few words (ideally 1-5 words), trusting the reader to fill in the blanks; score 0 if the caption is wordy, rambles, or over-explains the premise.

items.X_desc: Score how effectively the caption uses a precise number, proper name, or hyper-specific detail to make an absurd scenario feel real. A 10 means one exact detail anchors the entire fantasy in lived reality and amplifies the comedy. A 0 means the caption is vague or generic.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 if the caption cleverly plays off a highly specific, obscure detail drawn in the cartoon; score 0 if the caption ignores the specific details of the drawing and relies on generic tropes or makes factually mismatched claims about the image.

items.X_desc: Score 10 when the caption turns a bodily or social norm into a precise comic mechanism integrated with the image; score 0 when provocative language is gratuitous or unrelated.
items.Y_desc: Score how far the caption pushes beyond the cartoon's surface tone into darker, riskier, or more uncomfortable territory. A 10 means the caption introduces a genuinely shocking, morally troubling, or taboo subtext. A 0 means the caption is wholesome, safe, or tonally neutral.

items.X_desc: Give 10 when the caption finds a surprising but defensible angle instead of the most obvious observation or stock pun; give 0 when it is predictable, generic, or simply restates the premise.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 when the caption recasts the impossible scene as a coherent alternative situation or practical consequence; score 0 when it simply states that the depicted event is strange.

items.X_desc: Give 10 when the caption redirects the viewer from the obvious visual interpretation to a sharper alternative with a clear turn; give 0 when it merely labels the anomaly or supplies no reinterpretation.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 if the caption completely reframes the drawing by introducing an unexpected hidden motive or past/future event that changes the context of the scene; score 0 if the caption merely describes what is obviously happening in the drawing.

items.Y_desc: Rate 0-10 the extent to which the caption's primary joke mechanism is applying a common idiom or cliché literally to the visual elements of the drawing (e.g., 'cross word', 'pull the wool'). The judge must not judge whether the feature is good.

items.X_name: Caption narrates or explains the drawing rather than speaking inside it
items.X_desc: MODE 2 fingerprint. Score 0-10 for how much the caption RESTATES OR EXPLAINS what the cartoon description already says, instead of being a line a character would plausibly say in the moment. High scores for: naming the visible incongruity outright, telling the reader what to notice, glossing the situation, or supplying a caption that would be unintelligible if the reader could not see the drawing being described back to them. Low scores for: in-scene speech that presupposes the situation without describing it. 0 = pure in-scene utterance that never mentions what is visible; 10 = a sentence whose main content is a description of the picture. You must NOT judge whether explaining is a weakness or whether the line is funny; measure only the amount of drawing-restatement present.
items.Y_desc: Score 0-10 the extent to which the caption uses conversational filler, rhetorical questions, or multi-part sentence structures to over-explain the premise or set up the punchline. Do not judge quality.

items.X_desc: Score 0-10 for how much the caption uses the most immediate, conventional interpretation or pun invited by the drawing; do not judge whether that interpretation is good, funny, or apt.
items.Y_desc: Score 0-10 how much the caption reads like a standard, safe, well-formed pun or joke that any competent writer or general language model would immediately generate for the described scene. Explicitly do not judge whether the joke is actually good.

items.X_name: Obvious first-thought reading of the drawing
items.X_desc: 0-10: how much does the caption state the single most literal, first-thing-anyone-would-notice observation about the scene (the most obvious available pun or the most obvious mismatch/absurdity already named in the cartoon description) rather than an angle that requires a further inferential step? 0 = caption takes a distinctly non-obvious angle; 10 = the caption is the most generic, first-thought reading available for this scene. Score only how obvious/first-thought the reading is; do not judge whether that reading is well-written.
items.Y_desc: Score 0–10 for the extent to which the caption follows the most literal salient object, stock phrase, or immediately available pun suggested by the cartoon; judge predictability of the route, never quality.

items.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the extent to which the caption uses the cartoon’s single most salient object or word in a familiar pun or stock verbal association. Do not judge whether the pun is effective.
items.Y_desc: Score 0-10 how much the caption reads like a standard, safe, well-formed pun or joke that any competent writer or general language model would immediately generate for the described scene. Explicitly do not judge whether the joke is actually good.

items.X_name: Content outside the venue's printed register (bodily, sexual, injury, transgressive)
items.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT to which the caption's content sits outside the restrained register a general-audience magazine cartoon caption normally occupies. Add extent for: sexual or anatomical reference and double entendre; scatological or excretory wording; bodily injury, mutilation or death treated as the joke's material; language about consent, coercion or violence; and any wording whose bluntness would need an editor's second look. 0 = wholly mild and printable without comment; 10 = the caption's entire payload is transgressive material. Judge ONLY how far the content sits from the mild register. Do NOT judge whether the transgression is funny, offensive, tasteful or warranted; you are measuring distance from the house register, not approving or condemning it.
items.Y_desc: 0-10: how much does the caption contain sexual, off-color, or otherwise taboo/impolite content or innuendo, versus a fully family-friendly, decorous register? 0 = fully decorous, no off-color content; 10 = the caption is centrally built around risqué/taboo content. Score only the presence of such content; do not judge whether the risqué content is funny or tasteful.

items.X_name: Era-locked idiom dating the entry to a period of the series
items.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT to which the caption's vocabulary and references place it in a particular stretch of years rather than being period-neutral. Add extent for: pandemic-era public-health idiom (distancing measured in feet, shutdowns, immunity language, masking, remote work); named consumer technologies and platforms; slang or catchphrases whose currency is confined to a decade; and references to institutions or practices that have since changed. 0 = the wording would read the same in any decade; 10 = the line could be dated to within a couple of years from vocabulary alone. Judge ONLY period-specificity of the wording. Do NOT judge whether the reference is stale, timely, clever or appropriate.
items.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for how much the caption uses period-specific technology, slang, idiom, or cultural vocabulary; do not judge whether the wording is effective.

items.X_name: Uniform lowercase/no terminal punctuation transcription style
items.X_desc: 0-10: how fully does the caption follow a flattened transcription style — entirely lowercase (no capital letters anywhere, including at the start of the sentence or for proper nouns) and no terminal punctuation mark (no period, question mark, or exclamation point at the very end)? 0 = caption uses standard capitalization and/or ends with punctuation; 10 = caption is fully lowercase throughout with no closing punctuation mark. Score only this transcription pattern; do not judge whether the styling is appropriate.
items.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for the presence of mechanical formatting conventions such as lowercase openings, omitted terminal punctuation, doubled hyphens, or distinctive apostrophe and dash usage; do not judge whether the formatting is good.

anchors.X_name: Presence of a trailing apology or disclaimer
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for how fully the text ends with an apology, a disclaimer, an edit note or a plea to the reader. Extent only.
anchors.Y_name: Closing self-deprecating note to the reader
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for whether the writer signs off by apologising for the joke or hedging about it. Extent only; do not judge quality.

anchors.X_name: How much capitalised shouting the text contains
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the density of all-caps words and repeated exclamation marks. Count only; do not judge whether it is effective.
anchors.Y_name: How far the ending reinterprets the setup
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for whether the final move makes the reader re-read the setup with a second meaning. Judge the mechanism, not the typography.
